checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Can a P2P peer withhold cells to trigger incorrect polynomial recovery?

reachability.notes: An attacker withholds cells so that fewer than 50% are available. If the threshold check is bypassed, recovery produces an incorrect polynomial.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Identify the P2P gossip validation layer for cell transmission. 2. Determine how cells are collected from multiple peers before recovery. 3. Simulate a scenario where a malicious peer withholds cells such that < 50% are available. 4. Verify the recovery function rejects this input before attempting polynomial interpolation. 5. If rejection fails, verify the resulting polynomial is incorrect. 6. Check if incorrect proofs generated from this polynomial would be accepted downstream. 7. Verify attestation validity checks would catch corrupted data.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W5B14-14, Trust Boundary: tb-003, Nodes: actor-p2p-peer, actor-validator-node. Attacker withholds cells to produce incorrect recovery output.

Determine if incorrect cells/proofs would propagate through the network. 4. Check if validator attestations would be affected by incorrect recovery. 5. Verify if there are secondary validation layers that would detect corruption. 6. Assess consensus impact: could incorrect proofs cause chain splits or finality issues? 7. Document the full attack chain from cell withholding to network impact.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W5B14-14, Trust Boundary: tb-003. Bypassing threshold produces incorrect polynomial that generates incorrect cells and proofs propagating through the network.

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Is the cell count pre-condition checked before all other operations?

reachability.notes: An attacker withholds cells so that fewer than 50% are available. If the threshold check is bypassed, recovery produces an incorrect polynomial.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Review recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs function entry point. 2. Verify cell count check is the first validation after basic parameter parsing. 3. Ensure no allocations or cryptographic setup occurs before the threshold check. 4. Verify rejection returns immediately without partial processing. 5. Check that the function signature enforces input types that prevent bypassing the check. 6. Verify the pre-condition is documented in function specification.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W5B14-14, Trust Boundary: tb-003. Pre-condition must be checked before any resource-intensive operations.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are cell_indices validated for uniqueness and ascending order before polynomial recovery?

reachability.notes: An attacker provides duplicate cell_indices with conflicting cell data. If uniqueness is not enforced, polynomial interpolation produces incorrect results, and the recovered polynomial differs from the original.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Locate the recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs function and its entry point validation. 2. Identify where cell_indices is parsed and validated. 3. Verify uniqueness check: attempt to submit duplicate cell_indices (e.g., [0, 0, 1, 2]) and verify rejection. 4. Verify ascending order check: attempt to submit unsorted cell_indices (e.g., [2, 1, 0, 3]) and verify rejection. 5. Test edge cases: adjacent duplicates, non-adjacent duplicates, descending order, equal adjacent values. 6. Submit duplicate cell_indices with CONFLICTING cell data and verify: (a) rejection occurs before interpolation, (b) no partial processing or state changes. 7. Verify the error response does not leak internal state. 8. Check that validation happens before any cryptographic operations.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W5B14-15, Trust Boundary: tb-003. Duplicate/unsorted cell_indices with conflicting data causes incorrect polynomial interpolation.

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Does polynomial interpolation assume unique, sorted cell_indices?

reachability.notes: An attacker provides duplicate cell_indices with conflicting cell data. If uniqueness is not enforced, polynomial interpolation produces incorrect results, and the recovered polynomial differs from the original.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Review the polynomial interpolation algorithm used in recovery. 2. Identify any assumptions about input uniqueness or ordering in the interpolation code. 3. Determine if duplicate x-coordinates (cell_indices) would cause: division by zero, undefined behavior, or silent incorrect results. 4. Trace the data flow from cell_indices validation to interpolation call. 5. Verify no path exists where unvalidated cell_indices reach the interpolation function. 6. Check for defensive programming: does the interpolation function have its own validation? 7. Assess if memory safety issues could arise from duplicate indices (buffer overflows, out-of-bounds access).
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W5B14-15, Trust Boundary: tb-003. Polynomial interpolation requires unique x-coordinates; duplicates may cause undefined behavior.

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Can an attacker inject duplicate cell_indices via P2P gossip?

reachability.notes: An attacker provides duplicate cell_indices with conflicting cell data. If uniqueness is not enforced, polynomial interpolation produces incorrect results, and the recovered polynomial differs from the original.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Map the P2P message flow from peer to recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs. 2. Identify all validation layers between P2P reception and function call. 3. Check if P2P gossip validation includes cell_indices uniqueness check. 4. Verify validation cannot be bypassed by crafted P2P messages. 5. Test: craft a P2P message with duplicate cell_indices and conflicting cells. 6. Observe if the message reaches recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs. 7. Verify that network-level rate limiting exists to prevent flooding with malformed requests. 8. Check peer scoring: are peers sending duplicate cell_indices penalized?
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W5B14-15, Trust Boundary: tb-003. Attacker-controlled P2P input requires validation before processing.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are all cell_indices validated to be in [0, CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB) before polynomial recovery begins?

reachability.notes: Out-of-range cell indices would cause out-of-bounds access in coset computation functions.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Locate the recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs function (SG-024) entry point. 2. Identify where cell_indices array is parsed and validated. 3. Verify range check: each cell_index MUST be checked against [0, CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB). 4. Test boundary values: submit cell_index = 0 (valid), cell_index = CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB - 1 (valid), cell_index = CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB (invalid, must reject). 5. Test out-of-range values: submit cell_index = CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB + 1, cell_index = MAX_UINT64, negative values if applicable. 6. Verify rejection occurs BEFORE any polynomial recovery or cryptographic operations begin. 7. Verify rejection occurs BEFORE allocation of recovery data structures. 8. Check error handling: verify out-of-range indices produce clear error, not crash or undefined behavior. 9. Test with mixed valid/invalid indices: ensure one invalid index causes full rejection.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W5B14-16, Trust Boundary: tb-003, Source Invariant: SG-024:INV-004. Out-of-bounds cell indices cause crashes in coset_for_cell and related functions.

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Does coset_for_cell crash or produce undefined behavior with out-of-range cell_index?

reachability.notes: Out-of-range cell indices would cause out-of-bounds access in coset computation functions.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Locate the coset_for_cell function referenced in severity justification. 2. Analyze how cell_index is used: is it used as array index, in modular arithmetic, or domain computation? 3. If array index: verify bounds checking exists, identify array size and what happens on out-of-bounds access. 4. If modular arithmetic: verify no overflow or unexpected behavior with large cell_index values. 5. Test coset_for_cell directly (if possible in unit tests) with: CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB, CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB + 1, MAX_UINT64. 6. Check for defensive assertions within the function. 7. Trace call path: verify recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs MUST validate before calling coset_for_cell.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W5B14-16, Trust Boundary: tb-003. coset_for_cell is directly mentioned as crashing with out-of-range indices.

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Is cell_index range validation performed before resource allocation in recovery?

reachability.notes: Out-of-range cell indices would cause out-of-bounds access in coset computation functions.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Review recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs function structure. 2. Identify the order of operations: parameter parsing, validation, allocation, cryptographic operations. 3. Verify cell_index range check occurs BEFORE any memory allocation for recovery matrices. 4. Verify cell_index range check occurs BEFORE polynomial setup or coset computation. 5. Check for any lazy validation that could allow invalid indices to reach sensitive code paths. 6. Verify early return on validation failure with no side effects. 7. Ensure the pre-condition is documented in the function specification per invariant SG-024:INV-004.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W5B14-16, Trust Boundary: tb-003. Early validation prevents resource waste and crash.
